name: Africa
alt: A world map with a large landmass highlighted, straddling the equator with hot desert across its northern half.
facts: Home to the Sahara, the largest hot desert in the world.
This is the only continent that sits on the equator and stretches into both the Northern and Southern Hemispheres equally.
It has more countries than any other continent — over 50 of them.
It's the only continent where you can find penguins, lions, and gorillas all living in the wild.
The Nile, one of the longest rivers on Earth, flows through its northeastern corner.
Thousands of different languages are spoken across its many nations.
Its tallest peak is capped with snow even though it sits near the equator.
Fossils of some of the earliest known humans have been discovered here.

name: Antarctica
alt: A world map with the icy landmass at the very bottom of the globe highlighted.
facts: It's so cold that almost no people live here — but lots of penguins do!
This continent holds most of the world's fresh water, frozen into ice.
It has no permanent residents and no government of its own — scientists just visit to study it.
Hidden beneath its ice sheet are mountains, valleys, and even a few lakes that never freeze.
Winds here can blow stronger than almost anywhere else on Earth, sometimes over 100 miles per hour.
During the darkest months, the sun barely rises above the horizon at all.
Its ice sheet is so heavy that it presses the land underneath it down into a bowl shape.
Explorers from many countries share research stations here instead of any single nation claiming it.

name: Asia
alt: A world map with the largest landmass highlighted, stretching from the middle of the globe to its eastern edge.
facts: This is the biggest continent — more than half of all the people in the world live here.
It's home to Mount Everest, the tallest mountain on Earth.
It stretches so far that sunrise on its eastern edge happens hours before sunrise on its western edge.
It contains both the highest point on Earth and one of the lowest, just a few hundred miles apart.
More than 2,000 languages are spoken by people living here.
A wall built long ago, one of the longest structures ever made, stretches across its northern lands.
It includes vast deserts, dense rainforests, and some of the coldest inhabited places on the planet.
Many of the world's major rivers begin high up in its towering mountains.

name: Australia
alt: A world map with one highlighted island-sized landmass, surrounded entirely by ocean, off by itself.
facts: This is the only continent that is also just one country.
It's home to animals found almost nowhere else, like kangaroos and koalas.
It's the flattest continent, with no big mountain ranges like the others have.
Nearly all of its native mammals carry their babies in pouches.
A massive coral reef, the largest in the world, lies just off its northeastern coast.
Much of its interior is dry desert, often called the outback by the people who live there.
It's surrounded entirely by ocean and sits in the Southern Hemisphere.
Many of its plants and animals evolved in isolation, since it's been cut off from other landmasses for millions of years.

name: Europe
alt: A world map with a highlighted landmass made up of many small countries packed closely together.
facts: This continent packs more than 40 different countries close together.
It shares one giant landmass with Asia, though they're usually thought of as two different continents.
Many of its countries are small enough that you could drive across them in a single day.
It's bordered by a warm sea to the south and an icy ocean to the north.
A dramatic mountain range stretches across several of its countries.
Many of its capital cities are connected by fast trains that can cross borders in just a few hours.
It's home to thousands of castles built hundreds of years ago, many still standing today.
Despite being one of the smaller continents by land area, it has one of the largest populations.

name: North America
alt: A world map with a highlighted landmass spanning from icy northern land down to a narrow strip near the equator.
facts: This continent stretches all the way from icy Canada down to sunny Mexico.
It's home to the Great Lakes, which together hold about a fifth of the world's fresh surface water.
It has only three really big countries — Canada, the United States, and Mexico — plus many smaller ones in Central America and the Caribbean.
It stretches from frozen tundra in the far north to tropical beaches near the equator.
A powerful waterfall along its eastern border region is famous for its roaring mist.
A long mountain range runs down its western side for thousands of miles.
It's home to a giant canyon carved over millions of years by a single river.
Many different climates exist here, from snowy mountains to steamy swamps, sometimes just a day's drive apart.

name: South America
alt: A world map with a highlighted, triangle-shaped landmass south of a narrow strip of land, crossed by the equator.
facts: Home to the Amazon rainforest, the largest rainforest on Earth.
It's home to the Andes, the longest mountain range in the world.
The Amazon River that runs through it carries more water than any other river on Earth.
It's home to one of the driest deserts on Earth, where rain almost never falls.
Macaws, jaguars, and sloths are just a few of the animals that live in its rainforests.
Many of its countries share Spanish as a common language, while one of the largest speaks Portuguese.
Its western edge is lined almost entirely by a single long mountain range.
One of the highest large lakes in the world sits high up in its mountains.
